messages:
devon: PR #8421 is blocked by Conftest OPA check — policy 'vm_region_affinity' failed. I'm trying to scale the nv4b-gpu pool from 16 -> 24 in ap-southeast1 for nightly batch runs but we hit the policy gate during the freeze window. Need quick guidance or a short-term exemption.

lina: can you paste the Conftest output? curious which rule triggered.

opa-bot: policy check failed:
```
error: vm_region_affinity: resource 'google_compute_instance_pool.batch-gpu' violates region affinity: requested_region = "ap-southeast1"; allowed_regions = ["us-west2", "us-central1"]
allowed_by: false
```

devon: yeah, policy expects GPU pools to be in specific regions to reduce cross-region egress spend. This workload is latency-tolerant and currently needs ap-southeast1 to avoid a multi-hop data transfer from our AP data source. We discovered queue latency spikes when running in us-west2.

chris: hmm. Two parts: 1) freeze window is until Mon 09:00 PT so changes are supposed to be blocked; 2) we have a small precedent for emergency exceptions if customer-facing jobs are impacted. Is this customer-facing?
sre-oncall: not customer-facing, it's internal nightly feature tests but they're gating a release candidate — if they fail we might delay the deploy.

lina: what's the risk of carving out a dedicated ap-southeast1 subset without changing global policy? e.g., create pool with tag 'ci-canary-ephemeral' and limited TTL.
devon: plan was to update the terraform module to set pool count, but Conftest runs in CI pre-merge. I could push a separate PR that creates a short-lived pool with label + strict IAM, then delete after 48h. But the Conftest policy would still block creation unless we get an approval.

infra-approvals: @devon please open an exception request in the infra-approvals tracker and include justification, owner, rollback plan, and time window. We can fast-track a 4-hour exception if SRE signs off.

chris: @sre-oncall can you sign off on a 4-hour exception for an ephemeral pool used for RC tests? If yes, infra-approvals will mark it approved and we can merge.

sre-oncall: looked at perf graphs — nightly jobs spike latency by ~350ms when in us-west2, which causes flaky tests. I can sign off for a 4-hour window tomorrow 02:00–06:00 UTC provided:
- pool created with label ci-ephemeral:true
- max nodes = 8 (not 24)
- proactive monitoring + alert to #eng-oncall if queuing > 90th percentile

devon: ok I can do that. I'll open the exception ticket now and update the PR with the ticket link. I'll also reduce the requested size to 8 and add delete_after = "48h".

lina: also add a Conftest suppression comment pointing to the ticket so the CI knows it's approved, e.g., `# conftest:exception=INFRA-1234` — we have that pattern for temporary overrides.
devon: done: created INFRA-1234 in approvals with owner @devon, window 2026-03-20T02:00Z -> 2026-03-20T06:00Z, changes: create nv4b-ephemeral-aps1 pool (max 8), delete_after=48h. link: https://approvals.redwood.internal/INFRA-1234

infra-approvals: Reviewed. Fast-track approved by infra team lead. Marking exception active, will notify Conftest RBAC to allow creation for PR #8421 during approved window.

opa-bot: exception recorded: INFRA-1234. Temporary policy allowlist applied to repo redwood/infrastructure for rule vm_region_affinity between 2026-03-20T02:00Z and 2026-03-20T06:00Z.

chris: :thumbsup: run a canary with 2 instances first, then scale to 8 if stable. Keep an eye on egress metrics.
devon: will do. I'll trigger manual apply during the window and post terraform plan + apply logs here. Thanks everyone.

lina: nice — after this we should add a Conftest test to validate 'delete_after' label presence for ephemeral pools so they don't stick around.
sre-oncall: one more ask — add a Prometheus alert rule for GPU queue length > 0.85 quantile for 10m during the window so we can rollback fast.
devon: noted, adding alerts to the PR now. will report back after apply.
